name: Equatorial Guinea

findings.summary: State operator GETESA signed a six-month agreement with Huawei, overseen by the Vice President, to optimise and upgrade its mobile and internet network: capacity, data speeds, stability and equipment. Value undisclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor Huawei, so prc. Tier 3: Capmad calls it a signed contract with a named counterparty; Ecofin and TechAfrica only say 'agreement', and no value is disclosed, so tier 2 is arguable. Sources disagree on the signing date (9 vs 12 July 2026). Huawei is also mentioned as a possible partner for commercialising SEGESA's 2,000 km fibre network; not coded, as that is undecided.

findings.local_actor: Government of Equatorial Guinea; GITGE (state telecom infrastructure manager)
findings.summary: Government contracted Huawei Marine in 2015 to build the Ceiba-2 submarine cable linking Malabo and Bata with a branch to Kribi, Cameroon; financed by China Eximbank, it was inaugurated in June 2018 and is operated by GITGE.
findings.analyst_inference: Cable vendor Huawei Marine, so prc. Tier 5: AidData records completion (March 2017) and inauguration on 4 June 2018; Osiris reported the inauguration as scheduled. AidData gives a China Eximbank loan of about US$402m (face value), recorded here only as financing, not contract value. Length reported as 290 km (2015) or about 400 km (later). SubTel Forum item likely relays a Huawei release. Pre-2020; current service not confirmed this run.

findings.local_actor: GECOMSA (Muni), 51% Government of Equatorial Guinea / 49% ZTE
findings.summary: GECOMSA, a telecom operator jointly owned by the government (51%) and ZTE (49%), opened in February 2012, funded by a China Eximbank buyer's credit; by 2016 it was reportedly near bankruptcy and indebted in 2020.
findings.analyst_inference: ZTE is co-owner and, presumably, network vendor, so prc; ZTE's role as equipment supplier is inferred from the joint venture, not stated. Tier 5 as an operating national operator. Loan face value unknown. Pre-2020; current status of GECOMSA/Muni and ZTE's stake not confirmed.

findings.local_actor: Government of Equatorial Guinea (ministries and courts)
findings.summary: Government contracted Huawei to install video surveillance in ministries and courts, announced by state broadcaster TVGE; first phase of about 18 months to cover Malabo and Bata. Value not disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Huawei named as contractor and presumed system vendor, so prc. Tier 3 as a reported contract, but both sources relay the same Equatorial Guinean state TV (TVGE) announcement, no S1/S2 source, so not corroborated. Deployment progress unknown. Framed in reporting as following the Baltasar Ebang Engonga leak scandal.

facilities.null_reason: two searches (English, Spanish) found no data-centre or AI-campus project since 2023

silicon.null_reason: no dedicated search; no accelerator purchases surfaced in network, data-centre or AI searches

models.null_reason: one search found only a January 2026 Davos meeting between the President and Amini AI's Kate Kallot with no confirmed agreement; no frontier-provider partnership or national model

research_gaps: Was the GETESA-Huawei July 2026 agreement a binding contract, what is its value and financing, and does it cover RAN, core or both?
Radio/core vendor of GETESA's existing network and of GECOMSA (Muni); is GECOMSA still operating and does ZTE still hold 49%?
Who supplies Ceiba-1 and the ACE landing, and is Ceiba-2 still in service under GITGE?
Progress, value and financier of the Huawei ministries-and-courts video-surveillance contract (Nov 2024); any S1 award notice?
Outcome of the January 2026 Davos contact with Amini AI on sovereign data/AI: any MOU or project in Malabo?
Whether Huawei becomes technical partner for the planned SEGESA fibre-commercialisation company.
